vehicleUpdates.summary: Five-seat series hybrid: petrol generates electricity and motors drive the wheels. Related mixed three-seat evidence is promising, with specific centre-restraint limitations. This entry covers pre-MY26 Ti AWD.

battery.basis: Nissan Australia original AWD launch capacity; not a verified usable figure and not a plug-in driving battery.

observedConsumption.basis: Exact 2023 Ti AWD long-term review: approximately 10,000 km over five months, highway-heavy. Review separately reports 5.8 urban and 7.8 highway; not a lab figure or fleet average.

length.basis: Pre-MY26 Australian body length. MY26 is 4,690 mm and is excluded from this entry.

familyFit.summary: A related 2023 Ti-L AWD test demonstrates the mixed rear-facing/forward-facing target. Some ANCAP test restraints failed in particular positions; your three seats still need a fitting trial.
familyFit.row2: Two outboard ISOFIX pairs; three top tethers. Outer tethers on seatbacks; centre tether above boot.
familyFit.row3: No third row in this e-POWER configuration.
familyFit.testedSeats: BabyDrive names Adapt More, Achieve More and Versatile Folding Booster but its text is inconsistent about facing direction. Inspected photos show one rear-facing plus two forward-facing restraints; exact model-to-position assignment remains uncertain.
familyFit.buckleAccess: Daily booster buckle reach is unverified. ANCAP could not fit either of its tested boosters correctly in the centre; that does not invalidate a different tested booster.
familyFit.access: Exact Ti long-term family use reports easy rear-facing installation and 85-degree rear-door openings. Ti-L rear sunshades are not Ti equipment.
familyFit.ventilation: Original and MY 26 Australian specifications list rear air vents and tri-zone climate on Ti e-POWER. Ti-L rear sunshades in the test are not assumed on Ti.

vehicleUpdates.servicing: Pre-MY26: 12 months / 10,000 km, whichever first. Eligibility and prices depend on original retail date and VIN.
vehicleUpdates.batteryWarranty: Original five-year defect warranty applies subject to its booklet. No verified e-POWER retained-capacity guarantee. Current terms exclude gradual HEV capacity loss; confirm original-delivery terms.
inspection: Check VIN applicability and completion of REC-006653 / R26A5; inclusion in a VIN list does not prove the recall remains open.
Bring your one rear-facing and two forward-facing seats/boosters. Check each approved position, centre belt/tether routing and booster buckles with all three installed.
Check front-seat clearance in your real driving position; the published 182 cm test used a related Ti-L, not your own seat.
Obtain the original warranty booklet, Nissan-network history and written Nissan MORE eligibility. Independent servicing alone does not establish extended-cover eligibility.
Check the next 10,000 km service and written VIN price. A 2025 retail date can change flat-price eligibility; calendar registration year alone is insufficient.
Test sustained uphill drive for any hesitation or torque pulsing; a long-term reviewer observed this, but it is not a verified diagnosis or repair-frequency claim.
Budget for your chosen 91 RON minimum or recommended 95 RON fuel. Check tyre repair kit condition; no spare is supplied.

changes.text: Australian Ti and Ti-L e-POWER introduced as five-seat e-4ORCE AWD configurations.
FWD e-POWER ST-L, Ti and Ti-L added. Nissan’s seven-seat Rock Creek is petrol, not e-POWER.
MY26 changes styling/equipment, body length to 4,690 mm and servicing to 15,000 km/12 months. A separate Ti AWD MY26 configuration has not yet been audited.

gaps: Your exact mixed restraints, driver position and daily booster buckle access remain unconfirmed.
Original 2023/24 HEV battery exclusions need the delivered warranty booklet; current published new-vehicle terms are explicitly for retail from January 2025.
MY26 Ti AWD is outside this pre-MY26 entry and needs a separately audited configuration.
No verified Nissan installed major electrical/engine repair quote or actuarial annual repair average was located.

length.basis: Dated August 2026 MY26 PDF. Live web table retains 4,680 mm; use the dated sheet pending exact VIN confirmation.

observedConsumption.basis: GoAuto ST-L FWD launch-drive trip computer, New Zealand, October 2026. Australian-market coverage but not an Australian commuting test; another launch reviewer saw 6.5.

familyFit.summary: Mixed three-across evidence comes from the related 2023 Ti-L AWD, not this new ST-L FWD. The target needs a direct trial.
familyFit.row2: Current Australian MY 26 brochure explicitly lists two outboard ISOFIX positions and three top tethers. A 2023 Ti-L AWD fit test is related evidence, not a test of this FWD ST-L.
familyFit.row3: No third row in this e-POWER configuration.
familyFit.testedSeats: Related AWD photos show one rear-facing plus two forward-facing restraints. No direct ST-L FWD three-seat test was located.
familyFit.buckleAccess: No FWD booster buckle-access trial located. Related ANCAP centre-booster limitations warrant a careful trial.
familyFit.access: The related AWD cabin has wide rear doors; confirm actual ST-L FWD loading space with all three seats installed.
familyFit.ventilation: MY 26 ST-L specification lists second-row air vents and dual-zone climate control; no third row.

vehicleUpdates.servicing: MY26: 12 months / 15,000 km. Eligible first five scheduled services A$399 each; five-service / five-year limit and exclusions apply.
inspection: Install your complete mixed three-seat set before purchase; related AWD results do not confirm FWD ST-L fit or centre booster compatibility.
Check exact fuel label: dated MY26 PDF says 5.4 L/100 km while the web table says 5.3.
Check the compliance/build details and dimensions: MY26 PDF says 4,690 mm but the live web table retains 4,680 mm.
Confirm first five services / five-year eligibility and written Nissan MORE conditions; later services and NissanConnect after its complimentary period may cost extra.
Confirm the 670 kg braked tow limit, repair-kit provision and official VIN recall lookup. Do not assume an older AWD recall covers every new FWD car.
Ask Nissan or ANCAP to confirm FWD rating applicability: the public model page says all variants, but the downloadable table only explicitly names e-POWER 4WD.
gaps: No direct Australian ST-L FWD mixed three-seat test or daily booster buckle-access test located.
FWD battery kWh is not verified from an Australian maker source; the original AWD 2.1 kWh claim is not copied.
Dated MY26 PDF and live table conflict on fuel use (5.4 vs 5.3 L/100 km) and length (4,690 vs 4,680 mm).
ANCAP public page says all variants, but the downloadable applicability table does not explicitly name FWD e-POWER.
No FWD-specific owner aggregate, household insurance quote or installed major-repair quote was located.

ownershipUpdates.serviceInterval: Pre-MY26: 12 months / 10,000 km. MY26 FWD: 12 months / 15,000 km; whichever first.
ownershipUpdates.serviceBasis: Estimate at 15,000 km/year, mainly for pre-MY26 used AWD. RACQ 2024 related ST-L AWD budgets A$756/year. Original 2023 six visits total A$3,051 over 60,000 km, reached in four years at this distance. These historical caps support the allowance but are not today’s VIN quote. Eligible retail from January 2025 has A$399 initial visits; confirm remaining caps, due work and exclusions. Tyres and repairs are separate.

xtrail-stl-epower-fwd-2026.serviceBasis: Estimate at 15,000 km/year: first five eligible MY26 visits are A$399 each, limited to five services / five years. A$500 is a long-term planning allowance with an assumed post-cap buffer, not a ten-year cap. Wear, tyres, severe-use work and repairs are separate.

xtrail-ti-epower-awd.basis: L/100 km planning estimate, not the 6.1 ADR claim. AAA measured 6.7 in a related 2024 Ti-L AWD on 95 RON (6.4 urban / 7.3 motorway). Exact 2023 Ti five-month test averaged 7.4 with highway bias and reported 5.8 urban / 7.8 highway. Point reflects mixed use; bounds allow route/load differences. Minimum fuel remains 91 RON, with 95 recommended; selecting premium changes pump cost.

xtrail-stl-epower-fwd-2026.basis: L/100 km analyst planning estimate. New ST-L FWD launch trip computers reported 6.0 and 6.5 on New Zealand routes; 6.3 is a rounded midpoint, not an Australian fleet average. A$ or annual distance are not included in this rate. Bounds are assumed. Manufacturer combined claim remains separate (dated PDF 5.4; web 5.3).

warrantyCautions: Base cover is five years / unlimited km from first registration or service. Original 2023/24 booklet terms must be checked; the currently published new-vehicle terms explicitly apply to retail from January 2025.

Nissan MORE can extend eligible 2021-onward retail cars to ten years / 300,000 km, subject to Nissan-network service terms and transfer eligibility. The advertised re-entry deadline for 2021–24 cars previously serviced elsewhere was 31 December 2025 and has passed. Current section 3(e) permits discretionary written Nissan approval; obtain the VIN’s written status rather than assume a used car can re-enter now.
Current terms exclude gradual HEV battery capacity loss. LEAF nine-bar / eight-year capacity cover is not an e-POWER capacity promise. Normal wear, tyres and 12 V battery limitations remain relevant.

risks.title: Battery-controller recall
risks.detail: REC-006653 / R26A5 covers listed T33 e-POWER VINs, with possible loss of propulsion from LBC software. Check VIN and completion status.
risks.priceBasis: Official software reprogramming is free for affected VINs. This is not a replacement-battery price.
risks.warranty: VIN-specific recall remedy; claim through Nissan before paying independently.

risks.title: Out-of-cover battery, inverter or motor
risks.detail: A diagnosed failure may require specialist electrical repair. No verified Australian Nissan installed price or failure probability was located.
risks.priceBasis: Unavailable. Removed cross-brand Toyota event-price proxies because they do not establish Nissan repair charges. A real used AWD battery parts listing is shown separately.
risks.warranty: Check original defect cover, consumer guarantees and written service-activated eligibility. Gradual HEV capacity loss is excluded by current terms.

risks.title: Generator, turbo or engine diagnosis
risks.detail: The petrol generator and high-voltage system need diagnosis. One exact Ti long-term test described torque pulsing on an uphill commute without a confirmed cause.
risks.priceBasis: No verified Nissan Australian fitted repair quote. A different manufacturer’s reconditioned-engine price is not an e-POWER repair price.
risks.warranty: Covered manufacturing defects and recall work should be claimed first. Maintenance, wear and excluded damage are separate.

risks.title: Used AWD traction battery: parts only
risks.detail: T&H tag 32270 is listed in stock at A$2,266 including tax, from a 27,149 km T33 e-POWER AWD donor. Compatibility and health still need written confirmation.
risks.priceBasis: Current advertised used-part price. Diagnosis, freight, installation and commissioning are extra and unpriced. Does not establish FWD compatibility or a new-pack cost.
risks.warranty: Check manufacturer remedies and the seller’s written used-part terms first.

reviewUpdates.scope: ProductReview T33 Ti e-POWER AWD: 4.2/5 from four posts. Related 2023–25 Ti cohort only; no isolated new 2026 FWD owner sample. Self-selected reviews do not measure failure probability.
reviewUpdates.summary: Visible owners value the smooth electric-motor drive. One detailed MY 25 owner reports technology and after-sales frustrations; check the actual build and equipment.
negativeThemes: MY25 app/connectivity and map-update frustrations in one report
Individual concerns about engine noise, audio or lack of spare

expertReviews.scope: Australian-market press launch driven in New Zealand. Direct FWD grade review, not an Australian long-term reliability or child-seat trial. Its 650 kg tow claim conflicts with maker 670 kg; use maker.
expertReviews.verdict: Refined, intuitive family SUV, with fuel economy still behind stronger hybrids.
positiveThemes: Smooth electric-motor response and restrained driver-assistance alerts.
Comfortable, roomy cabin and useful physical controls.
negativeThemes: Five seats only and no spare tyre.
Low FWD towing limit and weaker laboratory efficiency than RAV4.

insuranceUpdates.basis: Published Budget Direct median annual comprehensive premium for a new X-Trail is A$1,300, first-time annual policies purchased 1 May 2025–1 May 2026, reported by Chasing Cars. This replaces the unrelated RAV4 proxy. The insurer cohort does not isolate e-POWER, Ti AWD, FWD or the reviewed grade; exact sample n and risk distribution are unavailable. Youi all-X-Trail mean A$1,181 is a separate mixed-generation/powertrain cross-check, not pooled with the median. Comprehensive cover only; CTP is separately included in registration. The budget and low/high bounds are household planning assumptions, not a personalised quote, insurer minimum/maximum or confidence interval. Address, drivers, excess, insured value and cover can change the premium. Replace with a like-for-like current quote; no arbitrary SUV or generation multiplier is applied.
insuranceUpdates.scope: New X-Trail policy median · e-POWER not isolated

tyreUpdates.basis: Budget aftermarket fitted-set estimate, not a retailer quote. TyrePoint Nexen N-Fera SU1 105W is A$219 each / A$876 four fitted on sale, including GST/balance/disposal (A$240 regular each); A$900 is a rounded planning value. Possible SUV freight and local stock need a final quote. Nissan Australian specifications confirm size; exact Ti load/speed remains unverified. This is a provisional replacement-price reference, subject to the actual placard. Life is a common 40,000 km planning assumption (25,000–60,000 km sensitivity), not a measured model or tyre average. Wear varies with tyre choice, driving, maintenance and vehicle; model-specific replacement averages were not verified. Annual allowance = set budget × annual km ÷ 40,000, rounded to A$10. Age/damage can require earlier replacement. Alignment is additional; actual placard, wheel package and local fitted quote must be checked. Matching size/load/speed does not establish equal braking, efficiency or durability.

Budget aftermarket anchor: Dynamo Hiscend-H MSU01 107W XL, A$185 each × 4 = A$740 fitted. Ordinary JAX advertised price includes fitting, balancing, tubeless valves, disposal, selected-store delivery and GST; no temporary multi-buy discount used. Store stock and Brisbane availability are unconfirmed. Life is a common 40,000 km planning assumption (25,000–60,000 km sensitivity), not a measured model or tyre average. Wear varies with tyre choice, driving, maintenance and vehicle; model-specific replacement averages were not verified. Annual allowance = set budget × annual km ÷ 40,000, rounded to A$10. Age/damage can require earlier replacement. Alignment is additional; actual placard, wheel package and local fitted quote must be checked. Matching size/load/speed does not establish equal braking, efficiency or durability.

fitAssessments.summary: Related 2023 Ti-L AWD mixed-restraint test; exact seats and daily buckles still need confirmation.

arrangement.detail: Photos demonstrate one rear-facing plus two forward-facing restraints in Ti-L AWD. ANCAP documents model-specific centre fit failures; this is not an any-three-seat guarantee.

buckles.detail: No daily booster buckle-access test for the mixed arrangement was located.

space.detail: A 182 cm driver fitted ahead of a rear-facing restraint in related Ti-L; exact Ti long-term use also reports easy rear-facing installation.

access.detail: Exact Ti long-term family use confirms wide doors and easy rear-facing loading.

fitAssessments.summary: Related AWD evidence only; new ST-L FWD has no direct mixed-restraint trial.

arrangement.detail: Photos demonstrate one rear-facing plus two forward-facing restraints in Ti-L AWD. ANCAP documents model-specific centre fit failures; this is not an any-three-seat guarantee.

buckles.detail: No daily booster buckle-access test for the mixed arrangement was located.

space.detail: The related Ti-L test had rear-facing clearance for a 182 cm driver. FWD ST-L seating/trim still requires a direct trial.

access.detail: Related AWD wide-opening doors help, but loaded ST-L FWD access has not been directly tested.

audit.summary: Mixed rear-facing fit evidence is more useful than the old generic three-across label, but centre restraint compatibility and exact buckles matter. Fuel budgets now separate observed AWD/FWD evidence. Old AWD is narrowed to pre-MY26; uncertain installed repair prices are no longer borrowed from other brands.

items.finding: Three new FWD physical stocks remain A$45,990 drive-away: QLD one, NSW two; known odometers 6–10 km. Motorama A$42,488 / 44,346 km and Gatton A$36,990 / 60,573 km match used data. Sunshine cached A$39,999 conflicts with the earlier same-day A$33,999 direct observation; fresh access was blocked. Keep existing asking snapshot, not a sale valuation.

Old AWD battery gap closed at manufacturer-published 2.1 kWh; usable energy is not verified. Rated AWD 6.1 L/100 km stays separate from observed 7.4 long-term Ti / 6.7 related AAA Ti-L. FWD planning use is 6.3; dated maker claim 5.4 conflicts with web 5.3. Both allow 91 RON and recommend 95; neither plugs in.

Related photos demonstrate the mixed target, but facing/model wording in the article conflicts. ANCAP found centre capsule, one rear-facing convertible and both tested boosters incompatible, plus one rear-facing ISOFIX convertible issue. Those are individual tests, not simultaneous three-across trials. Exact three-seat buckle access remains unknown.

Five-year base cover and conditional up-to-ten-year / 300,000 km service activation verified. Current full new-vehicle terms begin January 2025; obtain original older booklet. Retail-from-2021 eligibility requires Nissan-network servicing or written Nissan approval. HEV gradual capacity loss has no current warranty cover. The advertised 2021–24 re-entry deadline was 31 December 2025; current discretionary written approval is not automatic eligibility.

Used pre-MY26 A$750/year retained: 10,000 km interval, related RACQ A$756/year, historical six visits A$3,051. FWD A$500/year remains a planning buffer above eligible first five A$399 visits / five years, with 15,000 km interval. Neither long-term budget is a VIN-specific quote.

Insurance rechecked 18 October 2026: A$1,300/year planning budget; A$750–2,800 sensitivity, not guaranteed quotes. New X-Trail policy median · e-POWER not isolated. No unsupported SUV loading. Your drivers, excess, insured value and cover still need a quote; CTP is separate.

Budget aftermarket audit, 18 October 2026. 235/55R19 105W replacement reference: A$900 for four fitted; 235/60R18 107W XL replacement reference: A$740 for four fitted. Common 40,000 km life is an illustrative assumption, not model-specific wear evidence. Prices and annual savings are estimates; check the real placard and local fitted quote.

R26A5 software remedy is free for affected VINs. Real AWD donor battery is A$2,266 parts only; installed new battery, inverter or engine prices remain unavailable. Removed cross-brand major-event ranges. A$850 used / A$600 new annual funds remain savings assumptions, not measured repair averages.

Ti e-POWER owner aggregate still 4.2/5 from four self-selected posts, not FWD. Exact Ti professional long-term use adds highway-heavy fuel and practical evidence. New FWD has an Australian-publisher launch review from New Zealand; it cannot establish Australian ownership reliability.

Towing verified: AWD 1,650 kg, FWD 670 kg. Boot 575 L is to roof, not shelf-height VDA. MY26 dated length 4,690 mm conflicts with web 4,680; old AWD narrowed to 2023–25. Three-cylinder QLD annual rego + CTP A$782.15–798.15. FWD exact ANCAP table extension remains unverified.
